summary: Lake County, OR lookout built 1934 as a 20-ft L-5 tower; gone by the 1950s. The summit now holds a Forest Service communications site.

facts.status_note: Tower gone by the 1950s; the summit now holds a Forest Service communications site
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Fremont-Winema National Forest

events.note: 20-foot wooden L-5 tower, per the register and firelookout.com
Radio equipment installed at the lookout station and a new forest road completed nearby (Lake County Examiner, August 30, 1934, as quoted on Kemnow's page)
Gone by the 1950s per the register and firelookout.com; a 1948 station description still describes the tower; no removal date or method given
Registered May 20, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek
Forest Service decision signed 11/26/2018 reauthorizing special use permits for the Dead Indian Mountain Communications Site on the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com and the 1948 station description give 20 feet; a 1942 district memo gives 16 feet. The story reports both figures. The record's 3.7 m (about 12 ft) matches none of the sources, so the 20-foot figure is used in facts.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 3.7 m (about 12 ft) matches no source: 20 ft in the register, firelookout.com and the 1948 NGS station description; 16 ft in a 1942 memo. A human should check the record's source for 3.7. Record design was null; L-5 comes from the register and firelookout.com. No staffing names or dates in any source read. Public access is not established: the 2018 Forest Service page describes a communications site and says nothing about visitors. The 1948 station description places a survey mark at the tower base; the sources do not say whether it survives, so the story does not mention it.
